report:
PASS for the manuscript’s stated partial theorem. This is not acceptance of the original P16.4 completion criterion. No mathematical grants, ledger verdicts, or historical reading claims were used as evidence.

Established scope: complete non-Archimedean real-valued fields K of characteristic zero, including trivial, discrete and nondiscrete valuations; smooth geometrically integral projective X; an actual ample rational line bundle L; and the manuscript’s decreasing-FS-net definition of psh. In precisely this setting, all five assertions of the main theorem follow. The extended energy and E¹ statements concern actual scalar potentials defined by continuous-majorant infima. The measure dual uses continuous psh tests.

Field and quotient argument. I reconstructed finite-extension absolute-value existence using premises 1–2: a dominating valuation ring has finite-index value-group extension, which embeds uniquely into the divisible hull of the original real value group. This also handles a trivial valuation. For uniqueness, finite-dimensional norm equivalence over a complete field follows by induction using completeness and closedness of a codimension-one subspace. Comparing two extension norms on powers of an element then forces equality. Newton iteration also establishes the stated henselian background without a discreteness assumption.

For finite Galois E/K, H(x)⊗K E is a nonzero finite étale algebra, hence a product of finite separable fields. Each factor has one norm point. A proper orbit of factors would yield a nontrivial invariant idempotent, contradicting (H(x)⊗K E)^Gal(E/K)=H(x). This proves finite-level transitivity for every analytic point, including points with nonzero scheme-support kernel. The finite-fiber description follows by extending the downstairs seminorm first to its fraction field and then to its completed residue field.

The completion argument is valid. On a fixed affine chart, finitely supported coefficient differences have the displayed monomial bound. Numerical norms therefore converge independently of algebraic approximants. Relations in the extended defining ideal vanish by approximating their finite polynomial multipliers; this establishes independence of representatives. Multiplicativity passes to limits because convergent approximants have bounded seminorms. Localization at a function of nonzero seminorm gives the overlap compatibility. Thus the natural map to the finite-Galois inverse limit is a continuous bijection, and compactness makes it a homeomorphism. Surjective finite-level fiber transitions establish nonempty fibers. The closed matching sets F_E have the finite intersection property in G, proving transitivity on the completed fibers.

Joint continuity is also established for genuinely completed coefficients. Algebraic-coefficient evaluations have open stabilizers. On coordinate neighborhoods with bounded coordinate seminorms, algebraic approximations converge uniformly in both variables because every Galois automorphism is isometric and fixes the K-coordinates. These evaluations generate the affine seminorm topology. Consequently T is the compact Hausdorff orbit quotient, with the claimed continuous and upper-semicontinuous descent properties.

Psh descent. Rational convex combinations of FS metrics are obtained by clearing denominators and taking all tensor-product section pairs, with the corresponding summed weights. Uniform approximation establishes rational convexity for continuous psh metrics; approximation of a real coefficient then establishes real convexity. Compactness of the action supplies uniform finite-max approximations to each orbit maximum. Semilinear transport preserves FS systems, so finite maximum and uniform closure establish its psh property. The continuous field-recognition theorem applies to the actual descended metric: geometric reducedness, projectivity, semi-ampleness and completeness all hold.

The decreasing-net endpoint is exact. For every finite b>u_C(y), the compact sets Q_i decrease with empty intersection. Directedness turns the resulting finite subcover into an eventually empty Q_i. This proves inf_i h_i^G(y)=u_C(y), also when the endpoint is −∞. Decreasing closure then gives a downstairs psh metric in the original fixed-bundle FS-net definition. Surjectivity of π proves injectivity and order reflection. No singular field-recognition theorem, envelope continuity, or descent of individual FS coefficient lists is presumed.

Continuous energy and concavity. I reconstructed the first variation by multilinearity and integration by parts: the differentiated terms telescope to ∫h(dd^cφ_t)^n. Differentiating again gives n∫h dd^ch∧(dd^cφ_t)^(n−1). With d^c=(d''−d')/2, dh∧d^ch=d'h∧d''h is positive. Stokes gives the negative gradient integral, and the curvature factors and fundamental current preserve positivity. Uniform smooth regularization and uniform-to-weak continuity pass the inequality to continuous psh metrics and a continuous reference. Transporting tropical charts, their calibrations and fundamental classes under a valued-field automorphism establishes semilinear measure equivariance and energy invariance; uniform regularization extends both statements.

Extended energy. The compact-majorant lemma is correct for arbitrary directed decreasing nets. For any continuous majorant w and ε>0, the closed sets {v_i−w≥ε} decrease with empty intersection, giving eventual domination by w+ε. Monotonicity and the raw constant-shift law yield inf_i E(v_i)≤E(w)+Vε. Taking ε to zero and then the majorant infimum proves the asserted equality, including −∞. Applying this lemma to the same downstairs FS net and its pullback proves extended-energy descent. The reference-change formula uses identical sets of majorant metrics and subtracts a finite continuous relative energy, so E¹ membership is reference-independent. No unbounded product or integration of a directed net enters these proofs. The alternative orbit-max approach works by following a decreasing approximating net; it does not assert that orbit maximization decreases energy.

Radon lifts and duality. Probability Haar measure on the profinite group can itself be constructed from compatible normalized finite-quotient averages and Riesz representation. Compact joint continuity gives uniform approximation of Af by finite clopen-partition averages. The functional f↦∫overline(Af)dμ is positive, bounded, and has mass μ(T); Riesz therefore produces the lift. The same finite-average approximation proves invariance and uniqueness without an unjustified interchange of integrals. Continuous tests establish weak continuity in both directions. A finite transitive fiber has uniform probability 1/r, where r is the orbit size determined by the stabilizer; r need not equal the field degree.

For the continuous-test dual, finite convex averages remain psh, concavity makes their energy at least E_C(h), and invariance preserves their integrals. Uniform limits give the Haar-average inequality, and continuous field recognition descends that average. Together with pulled-back tests this proves equality of the two suprema, including infinite values. Singular psh scalars are upper semicontinuous and Borel; the nonnegative Borel pushforward identity follows from simple functions and monotone convergence. It establishes exactly the claimed equivalence for downstairs tests and invariant upstairs E¹ tests, with no conclusion for all noninvariant singular tests.

Continuous mixed measures. The scalar-extension pushforward law extends from smooth slots by uniform regularization and weak continuity. Equivariance and invariant slots make the upstairs measure invariant, so uniqueness of the Radon lift identifies it with the lift of the downstairs mixed measure. Intersection mass is unchanged by scalar extension and is V on both carriers. There is no field-degree factor.

Conditional observations and original scope. The mixed-operator reduction is valid under its explicit antecedent that an actual equivariant operator on all upstairs E¹ slots, with the required continuity and weighted identities, has been constructed. The solution-descent observation also correctly requires existence, equivariance and uniqueness of every upstairs solution modulo constants. Supremum normalization is legitimate for a nonidentically −∞ psh scalar with a continuous majorant. Neither antecedent is established by this manuscript. A dense value group remains an embedded dense subgroup in a valued extension, so completion of the algebraic closure does not make a nontrivial nondiscrete valuation discrete. A theorem restricted to a trivial valuation cannot supply the missing nontrivially valued theorem.

The unchanged original gaps remain: a genuine general unbounded mixed operator with approximation independence, weighted limits, locality and comparison; the envelope, normalized compactness, orthogonality and first-variation inputs needed by a full variational argument; and the intrinsic all-E¹ target condition, variational attainment and every-solution uniqueness. The original P16.4 completion criterion is therefore unmet by this manuscript and is not narrowed by this PASS.

Primary verification. Complete pertinent statement/proof units were independently opened and checked in [BE v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3): §§4.1, 7.1, Theorems 6.6, 7.14, 7.31, their pertinent FS/norm laws, §8.1 and Definition 9.13/Proposition 9.14. The proof of 6.6 includes the model estimate and both trivial-valuation cases; it supplies o(m), not exact equality of extended supnorms. [CLD v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v1), §§1.5, 3.12, 5.1–5.4 and Proposition 6.4.3, supplied the checked Stokes, positivity and mass foundations. [BGM v1 §1.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.03847v1) was checked as the stated continuous-concavity cross-check, not as a singular theorem. [Temkin v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1010.2235v2), §§5.1.1–5.1.2, matches premise 0; compactness can also be reconstructed from the finite projective unit-polydisc cover. The full proofs at Stacks tags 00IA and 0ASH and [Tao’s Theorem 24](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/03/02/245b-notes-12-continuous-functions-on-locally-compact-hausdorff-spaces/) were checked. Compact Hausdorff carriers satisfy the latter’s σ-compact hypothesis. Gubler’s restricted-field formulation was not imported as an unrestricted theorem. The indexed excerpts below identify these primary units; they are not substitutes for their complete statements and proofs.

Harmless corrections: replace ‘Compactness eliminates boundary terms’ by ‘Analytification is boundaryless, and properness supplies compact support.’ Correct the BE bibliography title to ‘Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry.’ In checking the source proofs, the uniform-closure argument uses a rapidly convergent subsequence, and the displayed difference in BE Lemma 8.6 requires a minus sign; its stated bound remains valid. None of these requires a substantial repair to the manuscript’s argument.

premises: For a finite-type scheme Z over a complete non-Archimedean real-valued field F, including trivial valuation, Z^an is obtained by gluing affine multiplicative-seminorm spaces extending |·|_F, with pointwise evaluation topology. Separated Z gives Hausdorff Z^an; projective Z gives compact Z^an; analytification is boundaryless over F.
Every local subring A of a field M is dominated by a valuation ring B whose fraction field is M (Stacks Project, Lemma 10.50.2).

For an injective local inclusion of valuation rings A⊂B with finite fraction-field extension M/F, the value-group index e=[Γ_B:Γ_A] and residue degree f=[κ_B:κ_A] are finite and satisfy ef≤[M:F] (Stacks Project, Lemma 15.125.2).

For projective Z over a complete non-Archimedean field and semiample Q-bundle A, the decreasing-FS-net psh cone is closed under finite maxima and decreasing limits; continuous psh metrics are uniform FS limits and uniform smooth semipositive limits (BE v3, Definition 7.2, Lemma 7.4, Corollaries 7.5–7.6, Theorem 7.14).
For geometrically reduced projective Z over complete valued F, continuous φ on a line bundle A satisfies d∞(∥·∥_{mφ_H},(∥·∥_{mφ})_H)=o(m) for every complete extension H/F (BE v3, Theorem 6.6).
For geometrically reduced projective Z over complete non-Archimedean F, continuous φ on semiample Q-bundle A is psh exactly when φ_H is psh, for every complete extension H/F (BE v3, Theorem 7.31).

On n-dimensional projective Z over a complete non-Archimedean field, continuous psh-regularizable metrics on Q-bundles A_1,…,A_n admit unique mixed Radon measures, symmetric and multiadditive, positive with mass (A_1⋯A_n), continuous from uniform to weak convergence, and compatible with complete scalar-extension pushforward (BE v3, Proposition 8.3, Theorem 8.4, Proposition 8.5).

For geometrically reduced projective Z over complete non-Archimedean F and continuous psh φ,ψ on semiample Q-bundle A, raw relative energy is monotone in φ, obeys cocycle and shift Vc laws, is V-Lipschitz in each metric, and is invariant under complete scalar extension, where V=(A^dim Z) (BE v3, Definition 9.13, Proposition 9.14).

On good Hausdorff non-Archimedean analytic spaces, including over trivially valued complete fields, CLD forms satisfy Stokes and Green with their stated support and boundary hypotheses. On boundaryless spaces the boundary terms vanish. For smooth real h, d'h∧d''h is strongly positive; products of semipositive (1,1)-forms are positive, and algebraic fundamental integration currents are positive (CLD v1, §§3.12, 5.1–5.4).

Every positive linear functional I on C(S,R), for compact Hausdorff S, is represented by a unique finite positive Radon measure λ, with λ(S)=I(1) (Riesz representation; Tao, 245B Notes 12, Theorem 24).
